Kilkenny Community Groups Receive funding for Climate Action Projects 
Kilkenny County Council and the Department of Environment, Climate and Communications are 
delighted to award €511,000 to 22 Kilkenny communities who will deliver a variety of local climate 
action projects.  
 
Following a very competitive process with a large number of applications received, these 22 groups 
were successful in obtaining funding under the Community Climate Action Programme. The objective 
of this programme is to support and empower communities to take climate action and build low carbon, 
sustainable communities which help to contribute to national climate and energy targets.  
Welcoming the funding, Cathaoirleach Cllr. Michael McCarthy said “This funding is a significant boost 
and recognition for communities in Kilkenny who are taking practical climate action measures in their areas. 
With these much-needed funds we hope to continue to see many more sustainable community initiatives being 
made in to a reality”. 
 
The projects funded include lighting upgrades on community buildings, bike shelters to encourage 
cycling, water fonts to reduce plastic bottle use, planting for wildlife, EV charging points at community 
facilities, community allotments, rainwater harvesting and much more.  The Climate Action Office of 
Kilkenny County Council will support the communities in the delivery of the projects and will share 
updates on the projects as they progress.  There will be another round of funding opening for the 
Community Climate Action Programme in the future. Kilkenny County Council are awaiting an update 
from the Department of Environment, Climate and Communications on this and details will be 
announced once confirmed.

National Food Waste Prevention Week 2nd to 9th June 2024 
During National Food Waste Recycling Week we aim to encourage everyone to recycle food waste by 
providing practical advice along with hints and tips on how easy it is to recycle and get everyone 
involved.

7 
 
The Environmental Department set up an information and awareness stand in McDonagh Junction 
Shopping Centre on Wednesday 5th June to highlight the proper use of the brown bin, provide 
information and advice about the service provision, how to compost and proper portion control in the 
household. 
 
Members of the public were also given a free brown bin on the day. 
Food waste is a big issue, as wasted food can sometimes end up in landfill, where it will produce 
methane which is a harmful greenhouse gas, this combined with the resources used to get the food to 
us, the consumers and then wasting this food can have significant impacts on the environment. The 
recycling of food waste diverts this important resource from landfill and allows it to be transformed 
into renewable energy and fertilizers for horticulture and agriculture use in Ireland.

Monday 27th May. 
 
This year’s “Team Up to Clean Up” will take place on the weekend of 20th to 22nd September 2024. 
 
 
 
The County-Wide Clean Up initiative brought together residents, businesses and local organisations to 
collaborate in a mass effort to enhance the cleanliness and sustainability of our County. 
 
Last year we saw over 200 groups register with over 500 volunteers participate. This culminated in a 
collection of just over 24 tonnes of litter.

The “Team Up to Clean Up” event created a sense of community ownership and pride by engaging 
participants in a variety of cleanup activities, awareness campaigns and environmental educational 
programmes.  It created a sense of ownership and focus for many communities, with significant 
additional interest by many groups and individuals outside of national campaigns such as the annual 
National Spring Clean which takes place during the month of April. All cohorts of society engaged

workshops.  Community groups, schools and residents committees can register via our online portal - 
cleanup.kilkenny.ie | Team Up To Clean Up - Together for Kilkenny

Works are progressing well on the construction of the replacement boardwalk at Lacken. This new bespoke

Budget 2025 
As part of the 2025 budget process the Elected Members will be required to make a decision on the base 
rate adjustment on Local Property Tax before early October. This item will be listed on the agenda for 
the September Council meeting. The ask from the Elected Members will be to maintain the same base 
rate adjustment that has been in place for the years 2020 to 2024 inclusive for the next three years. A 
separate report on the matter will be circulated to the Elected Members in advance of the September 
Council meeting.  The consultation period on setting the local adjustment factor for the Local Property 
Tax for 2025 will commence in late July and will run for a number of weeks.
